newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian PM Howard returns home from hospital.
newsitem.headline: Australian PM Howard returns home from hospital.

text.p: Australian Prime Minister John Howard returned home on Friday after spending a week in hospital where he was treated for pneumonia, a spokesman for Howard's office said.
"The prime minister has greatly improved in the last 24 hours," the spokesman told reporters.
Howard will spend another week resting at home.
Howard, who turned 58 last Saturday while he was in hospital, moved back to his Sydney residence, Kirribilli House.

Doctors examined Howard earlier on Friday and determined he had recovered sufficiently from his bout of pneumonia, which developed out of a bout of bronchitis and influenza, to continue recuperating at home.
Treasurer Peter Costello has been acting prime minister while Deputy Prime Minister Tim Fischer has been on a trade promotion trip in Japan.

Fischer said on Thursday he would cut short his Japan trip by a day and return on Saturday in light of the landslide at the Australian ski resort of Thredbo, where one body has been found and 19 people remain trapped.
Howard will miss a cabinet meeting on Tuesday to discuss Australia's chronically high unemployment problem.
"In the interests of a full recovery, Mr Howard has been advised that he should take another week before he returns to full duties," the spokesman said.
